acquisition method: Rapid shotgun and robust technology can now simultaneously characterize the human and microbiome contributions to the proteome of a body fluid
alkylation reagent: 10 mM tris (2-carboxyethyl) phosphine, 40 mM 2-chloroacetamide, 100 mM Tris buffer pH 8.5
alkylation concentration: 10 mM tris (2-carboxyethyl) phosphine, 40 mM 2-chloroacetamide, 100 mM Tris buffer pH 8.5
cleavage agent: a total of 20 μg of protein was digested by adding 0.4 μg trypsin and LysC to our lysis buffer
fractionation method: the resulting peptides were separated into eight fractions with basic reversed-phase chromatography
fragmentation method: The 15 most intense ions per MS scan were selected for higher-energy collisional dissociation (HCD) fragmentation
instrument: measured with a 100-min LC gradient on a Q Exactive HF mass spectrometer
ionization type: The chromatography was on-line coupled to a Q Exactive HF mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific) by applying a spray voltage of 2.2 kV
labeling: A scatter plot of the label-free quantification (LFQ) intensities of the proteins that were identified in both body fluids reveals little correlation
reduction reagent: 10 mM tris (2-carboxyethyl) phosphine, 40 mM 2-chloroacetamide, 100 mM Tris buffer pH 8.5
reduction concentration: 10 mM tris (2-carboxyethyl) phosphine, 40 mM 2-chloroacetamide, 100 mM Tris buffer pH 8.5
